reader.notes: ScreenReportPageIntegers sorts the written phrases into the canonical order and compares each with the next one written. Each omitted integer's GR2 default is a copy of a neighbour, so checking only the written integers also covers the defaulted pairs. At 85 the message cites §2023:13.18.39.3 SR6.

refuter.evidence: At --std 85: pgrev (FIRST DETAIL 3 HEADING 5, the phrases reversed) gives COBOL2744 'the HEADING integer 5 is greater than the FIRST DETAIL integer 3', exit 65. pghlim (PAGE 30 HEADING 40, so integer-3 defaults to 40 and integer-4 to 30) gives COBOL2744 'HEADING integer 40 is greater than the page limit 30', exit 65. pgfdneg (FIRST DETAIL -3) and pgfdpos (FIRST DETAIL +2) are refused by the grammar, exit 65. pgrevok (PAGE 30 FOOTING 20 LAST DETAIL 20 FIRST DETAIL 2 HEADING 1, written in reverse order) exit 0, OK. The pairwise check of the written integers in canonical order is equivalent to SR4 under the GR2 defaults, since each default copies a neighbour (OK §1985:XIII.3.8.4 GR2 'a value equal to integer-2 is given to integer-3'). OK §1985:XIII.3.8.3 SR4 'Integer-3 must be greater than or equal to integer-2'.
